(1) The JSON text is made once before the loop and the swap is one File.Replace with no backup, so the file is never wrong or half written. (2) Bounded at 6 tries, 40+80+120+160+200 = 600 ms; only IO and access-denied errors are retried; the last failure goes to the existing log-and-continue catch. (3) A 0.6 s worst case is acceptable: the normal cost is one 40 ms wait on a rare collision; the wait sits inside SettingsService _lock, which already serialised writes and stops two saves sharing the .tmp. (4) The temp file is used up on success (test 1 checks this); if every try fails it is left behind as before and overwritten next time. (5) Tests +41 -0, no existing assertion changed; the new test checks CD_Settings.json is byte-identical; no Settings key. 1023. **The three things that matter, the answer first.**
   1. **#1285 puts layout text and break lines in at model-space size.** Moving 25C text and BL into the layout you clicked is right, but both still size themselves from DIMSCALE. On an office drawing (DIMSCALE 100) a note typed on a layout comes out 250 mm tall on the sheet and the BL zigzag 200 mm (150 with #1278). Codex's recipe used DIMSCALE 1, so the test passes and a real job does not. Fix in entry 1026.
   2. **#1278 makes CEHATCH and CEHATCHAUDIT disagree at 1:50.** CEHATCH now places Earth at pattern scale 20 at 1:50, but CEHATCHAUDIT (and its repair) still expects the 1:20 value (8) at every scale except 1:100, so a hatch CEHATCH has just drawn is reported as wrong, and the audit repair would put it back to the 1:20 density. The new straight-line rule itself is safe: every shipped preset is either proportional (8/40, 1/5) or constant (1/1, 20/20, 50/50), so the line through the two stated values IS the proportional rule; it only "invents" a number for a custom preset. Fix in entry 1024.
   3. **#1282 may hand back the right style NAME with the wrong style VALUES.** The restore now makes the saved style current through the drawing (that part is the real BUG-621 cause: the old restore wrote the DIMSTYLE variable, which AutoCAD does not let a program set). It does not copy the style's values back (no `SetDimstyleData`, and not the `-DIMSTYLE Restore` the setup itself uses because "the command path is more reliable"), so Standard may come back carrying TIM LEADER's ByLayer colours and other settings as overrides. Not proved either way; Codex must read the next native dimension's colour and text height, not only the style name. Entry 1025.
1024. **#1278 @ cfaa62ca MERGE-WITH-FIXES, 1 MEDIUM, 3 LOW** (BUG-614/628: hatches and BL at any scale; switch `Layouts.FollowAnyDrawingScale`, ON). Right: one rule for the preview and the placement; 1:20 and 1:100 return exactly today's values; a mixed pair (50/1000) is still refused with a clearer line; BL is 1.5, 2 and 2 mm on paper at every scale (30/40/40 at 1:20, 150/200/200 at 1:100, unchanged); switch OFF gives today's behaviour. CEHATCHCHANGE uses the same `ResolveScale`, so it follows too. **MEDIUM (entry 1023.2):** `HatchUpgradeCommands.ResolveAuditScale` (CEHATCHAUDIT, its repair list and the closest-preset match) still uses the old two-scale rule; route it through `DrawingScaleRule.HatchPatternScale` with today's fall-back when that returns null, and add one test: a hatch placed at 50/500 audits as compliant. LOW: BL takes the annotation scale when DIMSCALE is 0 or 1, the hatches do not (they need the office pair), so "one rule" is two; and a model-space drawing left at DIMSCALE 1 and CANNOSCALE 1:1 now gets a 2-unit zigzag where it used to get 40. 1060. **The three things that matter, the answer first.**
   1. **#1304: typing F ends MLL/MLR and throws the note away.** The jig takes F, but AutoCAD's drag then returns "keyword" to the caller, and the caller treats anything but OK as Cancel: the note is disposed and the command ends silently. Before this PR F said "Invalid point" and kept the note; after it the typed words are lost. The repo's own jig with keywords (CDRG, `SourceBlockInsertCommands`) loops on the drag for exactly this reason. Fix in entry 1063.
   2. **#1300 fixes a cause nobody has proved.** It rebuilds the dimension picture (`RecomputeDimensionBlock`) after DSET, DSET1 and DUP set the factor, and reads the drawn number back to warn if it still disagrees. That is the right standard step, and the read-back is honest, but whether it cures the "still 5000 after REGEN and reopen" record is only provable in AutoCAD.
   3. **Two code clashes need a hand resolve:** #1300 onto #1264 in `DimensionCommands.cs` (four keep-both hunks), and **#1285 onto #1278 in `BreaklineCommands.cs` (new since round 2: a plain keep-both does NOT compile).** Exact resolutions in entry 1068.

   1. **#1317 (level cascade) does not work in Edit Pipe, the main way it is used.** Edit Pipe writes the new level onto the pipe BEFORE it asks "Recalculate downstream?", so the cascade reads the pit drop against the NEW level. Raise P1's arriving level from 10.00 to 10.20 (outlet 9.95): the "drop" is read as 250 mm and P2 to P3 stays at 9.95, so nothing downstream moves (today it goes to 10.20). Lower it to 9.80: the drop reads as minus 150 mm and the rulebook drop is used instead of the 50 mm the pit had. The builder's tests build the graph with the OLD level, which is the CDPROPAGATE case only. The switch is ON, so this would reach Tim. Fix in entry 1089.
   2. **#1331 hides downpipe junctions in metre drawings.** It now stores the downpipe's chainage in real millimetres, but the junction display (Pit Schedule, long section, Inspector) compares it with the pipe length in drawing units and drops any junction "past the end". In a metre drawing 12,500 against 30 means the junction wording vanishes. The Hunt said only the reported figure was wrong. Fix: convert for the words only. Entry 1103.
   3. **#1318 reads the pit's turn from the record, not the block.** The CD fit check uses the pit record's rotation, which is only written when CD places the pit or Edit Pit saves it. A pit turned with AutoCAD's ROTATE keeps its old record value, so the Hunt case (ROTATE a 600 x 900 pit 90 degrees) still passes a 750 pipe. Read the block's rotation (the pit id is already in hand). Entry 1090.

Fix: pass the edited pipe's OLD arriving level (`oldToInvertSnapshot` is already there) into the plan and use it for that pipe when working out the drop at the anchor pit; add a test whose graph holds the NEW level on the edited pipe (raise and lower), which fails today. **MEDIUM:** `RecomputeWithOverrides` (the preview's grade edits) rebuilds the plan without the anchor pipe (and, after the fix, without its old level); keep both on the plan. **(b) Rules:** R-08 drop comes from the rulebook (Settings-first); the BUG-654 refusal follows the existing flat-grade refusal and offers a way through, so it is not a new hard block, but in Edit Pipe there is no overwrite choice, so "run it again and choose to overwrite" cannot be done there (LOW 1: word it for each route).    2. **64e6751b (third look), the question Tim asked: does it really remove the 14 false R-06 rows on a downpipe marked Detention with an empty length?** **Yes, by reading, for the case run 33 showed.** R-06 runs when `RulebookEngine.IsDetentionPipe` is true. On 3.0.57 that is the pipe's own drawn type (its PIPE_LINK record, read by `ProjectDataService.ApplyCurrentRulebookPipeTypes`) when it can be read, and only otherwise twin tick or a real length. Edit Pipe on 1093C7 showed twin OFF (the window shows the stored tick OR a drawn twin, `PipeEditCommand.DataCollection` lines 76 and 127) and an empty length (the stored value), so on 3.0.57 the only way R-06 can fire on that pipe is a drawn type of Detention. That is exactly the case the new rule catches: drawn Detention, no real length, no twin tick, switch ON gives an Unknown row "marked as a detention pipe but no detention length is recorded, so its diameter was not checked (enter the length or untick Detention)". So the 14 rows leave "to look at" and join "not known": on that drawing CDCHECKS should read about 49 to look at and about 326 not known (the run 33 figures less and plus 14), if no other rule moves. Tim's settings file has no such key yet, so the default ON applies (checked: the JSON default keeps the initialiser true, and a missing Detention section reads true). **What it does NOT fix:** WHY 14 downpipes carry a drawn type of Detention (the fixture, or CE setting it when it turned 49 pipes into CE pipe objects on opening). The fit test "Settings fits 1920x1080 at 150% (dark)" passes in my full Civil run on the merged lane (it failed in 1548). **MEDIUM fixed:** retargeted to the installed C-58 line. **LOW fixed:** the start time is also kept under the command name, so a command that ends in another drawing still shows its time; `ACommandThatEndsInAnotherDrawing_StillShowsItsTime` cannot pass on 5ce7f6b3 (it printed "(time unknown)"). **The desk's five questions:** (1) **exact line:** `"Command outcome: " + NAME + " " + completed|cancelled|failed + " " + N + " ms"`, for example `Command outcome: CDSYNC completed 250 ms`; when the start was not seen it ends `(time unknown)`; pinned by `TheLineWording_IsStable`; written with `LoggingService.Info`, which is NOT gated by debug logging (only `Diagnostic` is), so it appears with diagnostics off. (2) **ONE place:** `CommandOutcomeLogService` hooks CommandWillStart, CommandEnded, CommandCancelled and CommandFailed on every open drawing (attached at start, on DocumentCreated and DocumentActivated; detached on DocumentToBeDestroyed and at shutdown). A command counts when CE's command registry knows its name or alias. I compared the registry with every `[CommandMethod]` in Civil: all 142 registry names and aliases are Civil commands except CEBLOCKS (a CE command too, so a line for it is right), no native AutoCAD name is in the registry, and only CE_TEST_RUN (the test hook) is left out. A guard fails if a Civil command is ever added without a registry row. Manager and Structural commands are not covered (their own plugins). (3) **no drawing name:** the line carries only the command's global name, the outcome and the milliseconds; CE's log prefix is time and level only; `TheLine_CarriesNoDrawingNameAndNoPath`. (4) **cost with the switch off:** per AutoCAD command one trim and upper-case of the name and one read of the cached Settings object, then return: no file, no drawing, no registry lookup. LOW (optional, not worth a fix round): read the switch before the trim. With it on, the line is queued to CE's background log writer, so the command never waits for the disk. (5) **cannot throw into a command:** every event handler and every logger method has its own catch; no transaction, system variable, command, selection or drawing write (source guard). Redo-safe: it writes only the log file. **Switch default, my recommendation: keep ON.** The "OFF unless the old behaviour is the bug" rule is for new behaviour that changes the drawing; this writes one log line and never touches the drawing, and the missing outcome line IS the defect. A key absent from Tim's settings file loads as ON (`TheSwitch_ShipsOn_..._AnOldSettingsFileKeepsItOn`), so once C-59 is installed the watcher sees outcome lines on Tim's PC on Thu 29 Oct with no Settings change. **What Tim will see:** a new tick "Log one line for each CE command that ends" on CDS > Advanced, under the diagnostic-logging tick, ticked; drawings behave exactly as before; CE's log gets one line per CE command. ## OPUS REVIEW OF #1520, BUG-859 DP1 DOUBLE-CLICK (Opus, Team, 22 Oct)

1588. **Thu 22 Oct 12:25 to 12:55 (real clock, Melbourne), Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Team, headless, desk plan/03. PR #1520 `b04/bug-859-dp1-doubleclick` head `3563aa9d` (ls-remote equal), base `claude/rel-20261020l` `33ef049e` (merge-base equal). Verdict: MERGE-WITH-FIXES. HIGH 0, MEDIUM 1, LOW 3.**
   1. **What Tim will see:** double-click the outer circle, the red centre or the angled DP text of a placed downpipe and CE's small Edit source window opens (tag DP1, Show label, Remove) instead of AutoCAD's Enhanced Attribute Editor. Cancel says "Nothing was changed." A double-click on a pit, a pit label or any other block with attributes still opens AutoCAD's own editor, as now. Turn Settings > double-click > source Edit window OFF and the downpipe goes back to AutoCAD's editor. The green DP label is unchanged (still in-place text editing).
   2. **The cause is right (read in the code, not only in the report).** `OnCommandWillStart` returned at `IsIntercepted(cmd, opensEditWindow)`: EATTEDIT is in the "switched only" column (`pit-label` and `source` rows), so with `doubleClick.opensEditWindow` OFF (`OpensEditWindowDefault = false`) it logged "left to AutoCAD: the double-click switch reads OFF" and stopped. `doubleClick.sourceEditWindow` was read only in `SourceTagCommand.ReadTagPromptsAndPrepareOrApplyLegacy`, after CDEDIT. With the shipped defaults the window could never open from a double-click. I could not open the Codex files CODEX_VERIFY_V4_20261022_0634.md and CODEX_VERIFY_V5_20261022_0835.md (not found under C:\CE_PLAN); I used the BUG-859 carpark entry, which quotes them (EATTEDIT dialog on circle, centre and DP text; TEXTEDIT on the green label).
   3. **The fix does what it says.** Gate: EATTEDIT now passes when `sourceEditWindow` is ON (`IsWatchedForSourceWindow`, EATTEDIT only, trimmed, any case). `NeedsRecentDoubleClick` still holds EATTEDIT, so a typed EATTEDIT, the ribbon button and Ctrl+1 keep AutoCAD's editor. `ShouldInspectDoubleClickCommand` still needs the compound setting (default ON). New step 0b in `ResolveCompoundRoot`, before the pit step: with the pit-label switch OFF the attribute editor resolves only to a `BlockReference` that carries a CE source tag (`IsTaggedSourceBlock`, which excludes pits); everything else returns null and AutoCAD's command goes ahead. Pit-label switch ON: 0b is skipped, the old path is unchanged. The pit-label behaviour is NOT turned on. Source switch OFF: the gate is exactly the base gate, so AutoCAD's editor opens untouched (CE returns before reading the selection). The default lives in one constant read by the setting, CDTAG and the gate (design rule 1).
   4. **No write before OK, protection, redo.** The resolve is a read-only open-close transaction. The window opens inside CDTAG after `TryCheckSourceProtection` (locked layer, Xref/overlay definition, locked label or hitbox: "CDTAG cannot change this source ... Nothing was changed"), and Cancel writes nothing. An untagged block is left alone: CE reads the pick, puts the same pick back (the BEDIT path already does this) and AutoCAD's EATTEDIT runs; CE adds no undo step, so a REDO is lost only to AutoCAD's own command, as today. A tagged source cancels EATTEDIT and starts CDEDIT (the drafter's double-click), same recipe as the pit and pipe redirects. Nothing unlocks or bypasses locked layers, Xref or REFEDIT. One U after OK: the #1499 write path, unchanged by this PR.
   5. **MEDIUM (fix before merge):** `TryRedirectToCdEdit` keeps the BUG-043 guard "no CE pits and no CE pipes in this drawing: bypass". A placed downpipe adds no pit or pipe record, so in a drawing whose only CE items are downpipes (roof plan laid out before the pits, or a fresh test copy) the double-click still opens AutoCAD's editor. It would also make a Codex probe on such a copy fail falsely. Exact fix for a Sonnet fixer: change `if (!hasCeEntities && !exactDbTextDoorwayOnly)` to `if (!hasCeEntities && !exactDbTextDoorwayOnly && !DoubleClickEditTable.IsWatchedForSourceWindow(cmd, sourceEditWindow))` (safe: with the pit-label switch OFF step 0b only ever returns a CE-tagged source, and a Structural drawing has none), plus a source-pin test in `Bug859SourceDoubleClickTests` that the guard carries that exemption, and one REGRESSION_LOG line.
   6. **LOW 1:** RED is by construction only (the new helpers did not exist). The bug condition itself is pinned: on the base `IsIntercepted("EATTEDIT", false)` is false, which the new test `ADownpipeDoubleClick_AttributeEditor_IsWatched_WithTheDefaultSettings` turns into the failing case. Acceptable; no further test needed.
   7. **LOW 2:** an attributed block that is not a source (a pit label, a title block) now passes through CE's read and pick re-set before AutoCAD's editor. Same read the BEDIT path has done since 3.0.51 and the comment says 2027 keeps the native target, but nobody has watched it on EATTEDIT: the Codex look should double-click one pit label and one title block and see AutoCAD's editor on the right block.
   8. **LOW 3, the report's "11 reds" claim:** checked by name. In a clean run only ONE test fails, on both heads: `BackTest_GlenEira24115_Computed_WithinTolerance` (known). Head 19,092 total, 19,072 pass, 19 skipped, 1 failed; base 33ef049e 19,074 total, 19,054 pass, 19 skipped, 1 failed; +18 = the new fixture. The report's other 10 (seven AppData path tests, two word-list tests, the 150% fit test) came from its redirected TEMP and log folder, not from the code. The claim "no new failures" is true; "11 fail" is its environment.
   9. **Green label (TEXTEDIT), recommendation:** a separate cause. The label is a plain DBText with no owner note, so `TryRedirectToCdEdit` treats it as plain text before any source test; even with every switch ON it stays TEXTEDIT. Recommend: log it as its own bug (BUG-860 is the next number) with a command card: a double-click on the label opens the same Edit source window ONLY when the two-sided proof holds (the block's own label record names this text), behind `sourceEditWindow`; plain TEXTEDIT otherwise. Not in #1520.
   10. **Pit-label switch and L4, recommendation (Tim's decision, not asked):** keep `doubleClick.opensEditWindow` default OFF in #1520. L4 is the same gate and the old behaviour (AutoCAD's editor on a pit label) is the defect, so ON is the right end state; but the EATTEDIT cancel-and-redirect has never been watched in real AutoCAD.
